text:
olga: FYI StratusPeak (SPK-120) flagged for collections. INV-2026-899 due 2026-06-10 unpaid $95,320. AP says they will pay but need the invoice reissued to parent company PeakHoldings LLC (different EIN) and want net-45. They offered to pay a 30% deposit today from the subsidiary account once reissued. Thoughts?
mike: Reissuing to a different legal entity mid-cycle is risky. We need a signed reissue request, W-9 for the US entity, and confirmation that the parent will assume liability. Also watch tax implications.
sarah: Sales chiming in: SPK is a renewal candidate. If we push hard, we might lose deal. 30% deposit + reissue seems reasonable if legal/finance get documentation. They want provisioning to continue.
jenn: Billing-bot: Last successful payment 2026-04-02. Charge attempt 2026-06-11 failed: CC decline. No prior disputes. Reattempt scheduled 2026-06-18.
legal: We can allow invoice reissue to parent but need an addendum: signed payment assumption form (Parent assumes outstanding liability) and PO or signed email from authorized signer. Also add clause that reissue does not change original payment terms unless we sign a new payment plan.
mike: Finance: If they pay deposit from subsidiary, we need payer remittance details and a matching bank trace. Also request the parent's legal name, EIN, and billing address to reissue. Recommend pausing new seat provisioning until deposit clears.
olga: Sales requests we keep core service running to avoid churn. Maybe suspend non-core features until documentation + deposit are received.
sales-bot: Sales note: customer is requesting reissue because their HQ AP requires centralized invoicing. They've provided a draft PO referencing INV-2026-899 but not signed.
jenn: Proposed operational steps: 1) Ask customer to sign payment-assumption form and provide W-9/EIN for PeakHoldings. 2) Customer wires or cards 30% deposit ($28,596) with remittance. 3) Redwood reissues invoice to PeakHoldings upon receipt of docs and clears deposit. 4) Pause non-core add-ons until deposit clears. 5) If no response in 7 business days, escalate to collections. Approve?
mike: Approve from Finance if we include following line in doc: "Acceptance of payment does not waive Redwood's right to collect any remaining balance from the originally invoiced entity if assumption docs are incomplete or later found invalid."
legal: Approve language. Also require that the signed assumption form include an indemnity for any tax exposure from reissuance.
olga: I'll draft customer email. Draft below, please sign-off: "Hi PeakHoldings / StratusPeak AP  to avoid service disruption while we process your request to reissue INV-2026-899, please: (1) upload a signed Payment Assumption Form and W-9/EIN for PeakHoldings LLC; (2) remit a 30% deposit ($28,596) via card or wire and include remittance; (3) provide a signed PO or authorized email confirming acceptance of reissued invoice. Once we receive docs and deposit, we'll reissue the invoice to PeakHoldings and resume non-core provisioning. If we don't receive docs or payment within 7 business days, we'll pause add-ons and resume collections. This payment does not waive Redwood's right to collect from the original invoiced entity until assumption is accepted in writing."
sarah: Looks good. Sales can nudge account owner but keep tone collaborative. Offer to waive one late fee if they submit deposit within 48 hours.
mike: Fine with fee waiver. Ensure finance records it.
jenn: Sending now to ap@peakholdings.com and ap@stratuspeak.io at 2026-06-12 15:04 UTC  Subject: Action required: INV-2026-899  reissue request & deposit. Will paste copy of sent email and attach payment link once processed.
olga: I'll monitor replies and upload docs to case file. If they accept, ops please coordinate reissue.
jen n: noted: reattempt scheduled 2026-06-18 per billing-bot.
